Self-Empowerment

Self-awareness, self-esteem, assertiveness and stress management for personal and professional growth.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define self-awareness, self-esteem and assertiveness
  • Describe assertive, aggressive and passive communication
  • List stress management techniques for nurses

In simple words

Self-empowerment means understanding yourself, valuing yourself and speaking up for yourself respectfully. For nurses, it supports confidence, good boundaries and resilience against burnout.

Self-awareness is knowing your own feelings, strengths and limits. Self-esteem is how much you value yourself. Assertiveness is expressing your needs clearly while respecting others.

Communication styles

Style Behaviour Example
Passive Gives in, avoids conflict “Whatever you want”
Aggressive Pushes own views, ignores others “Do it my way”
Assertive States own needs, respects others “I need a break; let’s cover each other”

Assertive communication uses “I” statements: “I feel…, I need…, I would like…”.

Self-esteem and self-awareness

  • High self-esteem helps nurses cope with criticism and stress.
  • Low self-esteem leads to self-doubt and difficulty saying no.
  • Self-awareness helps a nurse recognise when they are stressed and seek help.

Stress management for nurses

  • Take breaks and stay hydrated.
  • Use relaxation — deep breathing, mindfulness.
  • Talk to a trusted colleague or supervisor.
  • Maintain work–life balance.
  • Seek counselling if stress becomes overwhelming.

🔴 Assertive communication

Assertive = state your need clearly while respecting others. Use “I” statements: “I feel…, I need…, I would like…”.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Saying no — decline extra tasks politely when overloaded: “I cannot take on more right now; let’s redistribute.”
  • Asking for help — speak up when unsure about a procedure or patient.
  • Setting boundaries — keep the nurse–patient relationship professional.
  • Managing burnout — take breaks, use leave, talk to a supervisor.
  • Confidence — speak up in ward rounds and handovers with accurate information.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Self-awareness is knowing your feelings, strengths and limits.
  2. Self-esteem is how much you value yourself.
  3. Assertiveness states needs clearly while respecting others.
  4. Three styles: passive, aggressive and assertive.
  5. Assertive statements use "I feel…, I need…, I would like…".
  6. Stress management: breaks, relaxation, support, work–life balance.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Passive communication gives in; aggressive ignores others; assertive balances.
  2. High self-esteem helps cope with criticism and stress.
  3. Self-awareness helps a nurse recognise stress early.
  4. Professional boundaries protect the nurse–patient relationship.

📌 Memory trick

Assertive formula: “I feel…, I need…, I would like…” — three parts, respectful and clear.

60-second revision

  • Self-empowerment = self-awareness, self-esteem, assertiveness.
  • Passive gives in; aggressive pushes; assertive respects all.
  • “I” statements: I feel, I need, I would like.
  • Stress management: breaks, breathing, talk, balance, help.
  • Boundaries keep the relationship professional.

Test yourself

Assertive communication means:

Answer: C. Assertiveness balances your needs with respect for others.

An 'I' statement starts with:

Answer: B. 'I feel…, I need…, I would like…' is the assertive formula.

Self-awareness is:

Answer: B. Self-awareness means understanding your own emotions, strengths and weaknesses.

Passive communication:

Answer: B. Passive style gives in and avoids expressing one's own needs.

Burnout prevention for nurses includes:

Answer: B. Breaks, leave, support and work–life balance help prevent burnout.
